category: Core NLP Tasks and Structured Prediction
definition: Extracting structured facts (entity pairs with typed relations) and events (triggers with typed arguments and roles) from text.
details: Extracting structured facts (entity pairs with typed relations) and events (triggers with typed arguments and roles) from text. The pipeline that feeds knowledge graphs, and by extension GraphRAG-style retrieval systems.

explainer.lead: It turns unstructured text into typed facts — entity pairs with relations and events with triggers, arguments and roles. Those facts are what downstream knowledge graphs and GraphRAG-style retrieval systems are built from.

tiers.eli5: It reads a sentence and pulls out the who-did-what-to-whom, like turning a news story into a filled-in form with names, actions and roles.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run it as a pipeline over documents, then load the triples and event records into a graph. The common pitfall is error propagation: a missed or mistyped entity corrupts every relation attached to it.
tiers.paperLevel: Given text, output relations as (head entity, relation type, tail entity) and events as (trigger, event type, argument spans with roles). Limits: performance depends on schema coverage, and unseen relation or event types are typically missed.

explainer.example: From 'Acme, founded by Lee in 1998, acquired Beta', it yields (Acme, founded-by, Lee) and an acquisition event with Acme as acquirer, Beta as acquired, plus a date argument.
